brief.topic: A Bowl of Light and Its Return Journey

s01: A curved mirror can gather parallel light into one small place.
But not every curved shape does this exactly.
Look along this parabolic cross section.
Its surface changes direction smoothly from point to point.
At each point, light reflects at equal angles to the local normal.
Follow one ray toward the bowl.
The normal is the short line perpendicular to the surface here.
The reflected ray passes through the focus.
Move the meeting point, and the local tilt changes just enough.
The new ray reaches that same focus.
For this ideal parabola, every ray parallel to its axis shares that destination.
A three dimensional parabolic reflector uses the same geometry around its axis.
Real mirrors have imperfections, and this ray model leaves diffraction aside.
Place the source at the focus.
After reflection, these rays leave parallel to one another.
The same shape can gather light or send it outward in an orderly beam.

scenes.narration:
A curved mirror can gather parallel light into one small place. But not every curved shape does this exactly.

Look along this parabolic cross section. Its surface changes direction smoothly from point to point. At each point, light reflects at equal angles to the local normal.

Follow one ray toward the bowl. The normal is the short line perpendicular to the surface here. The reflected ray passes through the focus. Move the meeting point, and the local tilt changes just enough. The new ray reaches that same focus.

For this ideal parabola, every ray parallel to its axis shares that destination. A three dimensional parabolic reflector uses the same geometry around its axis. Real mirrors have imperfections, and this ray model leaves diffraction aside.

Now reverse the journey. Place the source at the focus. After reflection, these rays leave parallel to one another. The same shape can gather light or send it outward in an orderly beam.
